To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the even-odd properties of fission fragments are responsible for the even-odd features in prompt neutron and $\gamma$-ray emission.
the even-odd periodicity $\Delta Z\approx 5\approx\Delta A$ of prompt emission quantities is a consequence of the periodicity of the nuclear properties of even-Z and of odd-Z fragments.

the periodicity of the even- odd effect in prompt emission is due to the periodic nature of nuclear properties of fission fragments, and that the magnitude of the amplitudes of the even- and odd-Z oscillations in prompt emission is a reflection of the size of even-odd effect of Y(Z).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the even- odd effect in fission fragment properties and prompt neutron and gamma-ray emission.
the interplay between nuclear properties and the even-odd fission fragment distribution.
the interrelations between the global and local even-odd effects and the even-odd behaviour of nuclear properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the even-odd oscillations are the result of the even-occillations in the properties of the fissions fragments, which in turn are the result of nuclear shell effects.
the even-odd periodicity of nuclear structure properties, and not only of Y(Z), is responsible for the observed even-odd effects.

the size of the global even odd effect in fragment yields, as well as the size of the local even odd effect in prompt emission quantities are related to the nuclear properties of fission fragments and consequently to the nuclear properties which govern the even-odd character of nuclei.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of the even- odd effects in prompt emission, the nuclear properties of fission fragments are the key element.

the size of the global and local even-odd effects of prompt emission are determined by nuclear properties of fragments, while the size of the local evenodd effect in fragment yield depends on the even-odd character of fissioning nuclei.
the even-odd oscillations with a periodic $\Delta A\sim 5$ mass units in prompt emission quantities are a direct manifestation of nuclear properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the even-odd properties in prompt emission can be understood in terms of the even- odd effect in the fission fragment distribution.
the even-odd oscillations in Y(A) are not a mere consequence of the even-odness of Y(Z).
the even-odd oscillations are not an artifact of the statistical model.
